numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Probit log-likelihood is computed as log(clip(cdf(z), FLOAT_EPS, 1)), so every observation with q*XB below about -8 contributes the constant log(eps) = -36.04 instead of log(Phi(z)); for the reproducer model.loglike(params) returns -155.934 where the exact value is -1924.904. The score uses the same clipped cdf in the inverse Mills ratio pdf/cdf, so its value is ~0 for those observations (model.score returns [-4.874, 7.393] vs exact [-64.891, -2393.273], wrong sign on slope). Hessian and hessian_factor do not clip and return nan below z = -38 (np.isnan(model.hessian(params)).any() is True). fit(method="bfgs") stops at params [-0.036, 1.72] with bse [nan, nan] and llf -155.067, instead of the exact optimum [-0.129, 0.077] with llf -202.674.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: log(Phi(z)) should be computed via scipy log_ndtr (equivalently norm.logcdf), and the inverse Mills ratio via exp(logpdf - log_ndtr), so loglike equals stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum() (-1924.904 in the reproducer), score equals the exact [-64.891, -2393.273], hessian stays finite, and bfgs converges to [-0.129, 0.077] with llf -202.674 and finite bse.
trigger_conditions: An extreme, misclassified observation in the sample so that q * XB is far negative (below about -8 for loglike/score, below about -38 for hessian)
Probit model fit with gradient-based optimizer such as method="bfgs"

input_output_examples.input: Probit reproducer: n=300, rng=np.random.default_rng(1), one appended observation x=40.0, y=0, params=np.array([0.0, 1.5])

oracle_clues: Reference values are scipy log_ndtr / norm.logcdf and norm.logpdf (same as R pnorm(log.p=TRUE) and dnorm(log=TRUE)), per PR#10229

numerical_characteristics.precision: The clipped cdf is flat at log(FLOAT_EPS) for q*XB below about -8 and log(cdf) underflows to -inf below about -38; the log_ndtr-based computation is described as exact; the test asserts assert_allclose against stats.norm.logcdf with default tolerances shown partially only.
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Linear predictor q*XB around -38 or below (extreme misclassified observation at x=40 with params [0.0, 1.5]); test grid z from -1e4 to 1e4 with 50 points.
category_specific_evidence: Correctness violated: loglike should equal sum of log(Phi(q*XB)) (stats.norm.logcdf(z).sum()), but model.loglike returned -155.934 versus exact -1924.904 in the reproducer.
Score violated: model.score returned [-4.874, 7.393] versus exact [-64.891, -2393.273], a wrong-signed score per the commit message.
Hessian returns nan for params where some q*XB < -38; model.hessian(params) isnan any printed True.
BFGS fit returned params [-0.036, 1.72] with bse [nan, nan] and llf -155.067, while the exact optimum is [-0.129, 0.077] with llf -202.674.
Mills ratio formula used for the fix: score uses q*pdf(q*XB)/cdf(q*XB), replaced by q*_norm_mills(q*XB); reference computed as exp(logpdf - log_ndtr).
Clipping in original code: np.clip(cdf, FLOAT_EPS, 1 - FLOAT_EPS) made loglike flat at log(eps) for z below about -8.
Test test_probit_loglikeobs_extreme_linpred asserts finite loglikeobs, score_obs, hessian under warnings set to error, and loglikeobs close to stats.norm.logcdf.
reproduction_risks: The reproducer's exact-value comparisons are truncated in some passages, so full expected values beyond those printed are not available.
Test tolerance in test_probit_loglikeobs_extreme_linpred is cut off, so the rtol/atol is unknown.
Reproduction requires an extreme observation (x=40) to trigger the clipping and underflow regimes; without it the bug may not appear.
Outputs depend on random seed default_rng(1) and the specific data generation.
